# Decision Trees and k-Nearest Neighbors

## Overview
Decision trees and k-Nearest Neighbors are intuitive models that work very differently from regression. A decision tree makes predictions by asking a series of yes/no questions about the features, splitting the data at each node to make the resulting groups as 'pure' as possible (measured by Gini impurity or entropy), until it reaches a leaf that gives the prediction. Trees are easy to visualize and require no feature scaling, but they tend to overfit: a deep tree can memorize the training data and fail on new data, which is why you limit depth or prune the tree. k-Nearest Neighbors is even simpler in concept: to classify a new point, it looks at the k closest training points (by a distance metric like Euclidean distance) and takes a majority vote. It's a 'lazy' learner that stores all the data and does the work at prediction time. Choosing k matters: too small and it's noisy, too large and it blurs the boundaries. Both models help you build intuition for how different algorithms carve up the feature space.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Decision tree structure and splitting; Gini impurity and entropy; Tree depth and overfitting; k-Nearest Neighbors algorithm; Choosing k and distance metrics. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Train a decision tree and a k-NN classifier on the same dataset, visualize the tree, experiment with tree depth and k values, and observe how each affects training vs test accuracy.
Mini Project: Build a comparison notebook that tunes tree depth and k on a classification dataset, plots how accuracy changes with each hyperparameter, and identifies the overfitting point.
Assignment: Train a decision tree at three different depths and write a short explanation of how depth relates to overfitting, supported by your train/test accuracy numbers.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
